predecessors.name: Kingdom of Singapura
predecessors.text: Singapore island, which Parameswara left in 1398 and which Malacca later 'absorbed' as a Laksamana's fiefdom (undated); nothing passed in 1400

successors.name: Sultanate of Johor
successors.text: the south of the peninsula by the Johor River, where Alauddin Riayat Shah II 'established a new capital' in 1528 (Johor Sultanate page: 'founded in 1528 ... based at Pekan Tua')

successors.name: Sultanate of Perak
successors.text: the north of the peninsula, where Muzaffar Shah 'was invited to rule'

ledger.x: c. 1400: Parameswara, driven from Singapura, founds Malacca. Infobox 'Founding: c. 1400'; the Kingdom of Singapura page: 'Parameswara, fled to the west coast of the Malay Peninsula to establish the Malacca Sultanate in 1400'. The page says earlier dates have been proposed.
1405: the Ming open tributary relations with Malacca.
By 1424: Megat Iskandar Shah's control spreads along the Malacca coast.
1454: Malacca conquers Pahang.
By 1459: Muzaffar Shah's reign brings the west coast from the Dindings to Johor into the realm; he was 'the first Malaccan ruler to hold authority over both ends of the peninsula'.
1470: Pahang stops being governed directly from Malacca.
1470: Pahang becomes Malacca's vassal.
By 1477: under Mansur Shah the Dindings coast, Perak and Bernam, Rupat, Singapore and Bintan are held.
By 1477: Mansur Shah receives Indragiri, Jambi, Tungkal and Siantan when Majapahit's king 'agreed to marry off his daughter' to him (the Mansur Shah page names only Siantan and Indragiri as dowry).
By 1477: 'Mansur Shah was also able to vassalise Siak in Sumatra.'
By 1488: Alauddin Riayat Shah 'extended the conquests of his father to include the Riau-Lingga islands'.
1506: Malacca conquers Kelantan.

1511: Mahmud Shah withdraws from Malacca to a camp at the Muar River mouth, then (forced out in 1512) to Pahang as a guest, then to Bintan (infobox 'Bintan (1511-1526)'); the dossier puts the move to Bintan at 1513.

1511: the sultan camps 'at the mouth of the Muar River' and waits for the Portuguese to leave; the page says only that 'in May' the Portuguese with over 2,000 local allies forced him out, and Albuquerque left in January 1512.
1511: Pahang ceases to be Malacca's vassal.
1511: Kampar becomes independent.
1511: the provinces do not follow the fallen sultan.
1511: the tribute to the Ming lapses with the fall.
1511: the Portuguese take Malacca.

1511: the Siak tie is closed here by bridging: the Capture infobox gives 'independence of Kampar, Pahang, and others' without naming Siak, and the Malacca page says the former vassals 'were no longer paying homage' to Mahmud Shah after the fall.
1513: Mahmud Shah makes Bintan his base.
1513: Mahmud Shah's court settles on Bintan (infobox 'Bintan (1511-1526)'); the year is the researcher's reading.
1526: the Portuguese 'devastated Bintan in 1526', ending the raids on Portuguese Malacca; the sultan retreats to Kampar.
1526: the Portuguese raze Bintan and give it back to its previous ruler.
1526: Mahmud Shah retreats to Kampar, Sumatra, and rules in exile there.
1526: the exile court takes refuge in Kampar.
1528: Alauddin Riayat Shah II founds Johor.
1528: Muzaffar Shah is invited to rule Perak.
1528: Mahmud Shah dies at Kampar and the sultanate is partitioned into Johor and Perak (infobox 'Partition: 1528'); the Capture page gives his death as 1527.

wars.name: Ayutthaya invasions of Malacca
wars.outcome: Malacca repelled a land invasion in 1446, a sea attack in 1456 (its navy chased the Siamese back to Singapura) and an abortive invasion c.

wars.name: Malaccan conquest of Pahang
wars.outcome: Malacca conquered Pahang in 1454 and installed Tun Hamzah as governor.

wars.name: Capture of Malacca (1511)
wars.outcome: Portuguese victory on 15 August 1511 (infobox; 24 August in the Portuguese Malacca text); the city stayed Portuguese for 130 years.

wars.name: Exiled sultan's war on Portuguese Malacca
wars.outcome: Raids and counter-raids from the Muar camp, Pahang and Bintan; the Portuguese razed Bintan in 1526 and the sultan withdrew to Kampar.

certainty.note: A port polity whose reach is a list of coasts, islands and river mouths (Kuala Linggi to Kuala Kesang, the Dindings to Johor, Siak, Kampar, Riau-Lingga); no treaty line or survey exists, and after 1511 the exile court's real control is…
